notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/favoritetoggle.guide.tsx, self-contained) and docs/evidence/favoritetoggle.md at 4e470cf (“docs: adopt Biscuit's main at 3795b4c (v0.1.78-3795b4c)”, 2 October), the commit the copy snapshot records; both files are the same blobs on main and docs-next and unchanged since. The evidence has two dated parts: Checked, Sources, Contract, Rendered, Limits and Verification from 28 September 2026 on jfs-components 0.1.60, and a “0.1.78 check” from 1 October 2026 on mirror tag v0.1.78 (Biscuit's fix/component-bugs-v0.1.78 at 5b6894b); the guide's Sources note (“Checked 1 October 2026”, 0.1.78) belongs to the second. Every evidence and Sources item here cites the 1 October check, so it carries 2026-10-01 and 0.1.78-5b6894b; the trace check compares the version (0.1.78), so none of them is flagged. Nothing is taken from the 0.1.60 sections: the 0.1.78 check supersedes their Rendered and Limits lines (Active colours fixed as #168, size default M, aria-checked emitted, hit slop set), and their Contract loading line is out of date (below). Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). FavoriteToggle.tsx is blob d1bbbfd at v0.1.78, v0.1.78-636f3f5 and -c1fa197 and blob b3f5873 at -a116616 and -dbe0e02 (the installed file); its one change since the 1 October check is line 231, visible={loading === true} on the loading Skeleton (commit 8e2a35e, 17 October). The favoriteToggle/*, color/favoriteToggle/* and blur/minimal variables and the Favorite Toggle Size and Favorite Toggle Color collections are identical in the v0.1.78 and dbe0e02 token files. Every guide sentence quoted here was read against the installed FavoriteToggle.tsx (read, not rendered), with token values through the package's own getVariableByName (lib/commonjs): Favorite Toggle Size S, M and L resolve favoriteToggle/width and height to 14, 29 and 41 px and the icon to 10, 20 and 28 px; the collection's default is S, but the component puts Favorite Toggle Size M ahead of the caller's modes (DEFAULT_SIZE_MODE, lines 70–71 and 97–100), so with no size it is 29 × 29, as the Sources note and the 0.1.78 check say; favoriteToggle/icon/radius is 9999, a circle (103–107); width and height come only from that token (199–201), so it never stretches. Colour: the component sets Favorite Toggle Color from isActive after the caller's modes (114–117), so a value passed in modes is replaced; Active resolves background rgb(255, 255, 255) and icon rgb(206, 161, 90) (gold) in Light, and Default rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2) and white, as the 0.1.78 check records; not saved draws a light GlassFill blur with that 20 % white overlay behind a transparent container (206, 253–260), saved paints the white background with no glass. So the States copy (frosted circle and white heart; white circle and gold heart, as in Figma) holds. Disabled: opacity 0.5 (210), presses ignored (191, 242), and on the web tabIndex −1 (web-platform-utils.ts 283–291; react-native-web 0.21.2 Pressable also gives a disabled Pressable tabIndex −1, exports/Pressable 118–122), so “Dimmed to half opacity and skipped by keyboard focus.” holds. A pressed toggle drops to opacity 0.7 (68, 218); no guide sentence covers it, so it is not recorded. Loading: isLoading is loading ?? the SkeletonGroup's active (174–175), and it returns a Skeleton kind other of the toggle's size and radius (223–233), so “A same-size circle holds the place while the item loads.” holds. Since 17 October the Skeleton gets visible={loading === true}, and Skeleton.tsx draws when the group is active or visible is set (134, 272–275), so loading true now draws the placeholder with no group. That contradicts the evidence's 0.1.60 Contract line “`loading` renders a same-size circular skeleton only inside `<SkeletonGroup loading>`; on its own it renders nothing.” (true on 5b6894b too, which did not pass visible); the line is not quoted, the loading rule rests on the package's own loading fact (its JSDoc), and the evidence fix is in reviews/favoritetoggle.json. The guide's own Loading specimen wraps loading in a SkeletonGroup, which still works. Accessibility on the web: role switch (238), aria-label from accessibilityLabel or “Favorite” (187, 193; web-platform-utils.ts 198–201), aria-checked from isActive set after the web props (248–250), Enter and Space press it (useKeyboardNavigation, web-platform-utils.ts 115–141); the heart icon is hidden from assistive tech (265–266). Tap area: touchHitSlop gives (44 − size) / 2 on each side (86–89, 197, 245), so on phones the tap area is 44 px for S, M and L; react-native-web 0.21.2 never reads hitSlop (its View forwards only listed props and none is hitSlop; only the legacy Touchable mixin mentions it), so in a browser the tap area is the visible circle, as the Sizing description, the Sources note and the 0.1.78 check say. That is recorded as a gap and filed as Component Bug #541 (coordinator, batch 14). Not counted as a Coin gap, per the pack's rules (screen-reader names): on iOS and Android the Pressable gets accessibilityLabel undefined (239) and the label reaches only the web's aria-label (getWebAccessibilityProps returns nothing off the web), so by the source a native screen reader gets no name from accessibilityLabel; the Content rule to give it a label that names the item is still quoted, since it holds on the web and is the guide's intent. Out of date in the guide, so not quoted: the Anatomy note “Filled heart; its colour is meant to change when saved.” was written while Active colours did not resolve (0.1.60); since #168 the colour does change, white to gold (114–123). The Heart part rests on the package's icon fact instead (“only its color changes with state (white when inactive, gold when active)”). Both guide fixes are in reviews/favoritetoggle.json (human flag on the whole entry). Facts: the Favorite Toggle Size mode fact's generated default is the collection's, S, which is not what FavoriteToggle draws; the 0.1.78 check's line sets it to M as an evidence fact. Favorite Toggle Color and isActive get the 0.1.78 check's Active colours and aria-checked lines. Not recorded: defaultActive and the uncontrolled use (the guide controls every toggle from the screen), onPress (raw press handler), accessibilityHint, accessibilityState, webAccessibilityProps, testID and the inherited SafePressableProps, style (the building rules keep style off Coin components), Color Mode (building rules; in Dark the Active heart resolves to rgb(143, 99, 23)), the pressed opacity, the Storybook story list (Default, States, Disabled), the Figma node ids, the measured-size labels and the playground. The Sources note's “Declared and installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 from the team’s private package repository.” is not quoted (it says where the package came from, not how to use the toggle). Anatomy: Glass surface is the circle, always present (frosted while not saved, white once saved, per States); Heart is always present. Configuration keeps Size as the only look (contextual: saved, disabled and loading are states, and the icon prop is for future reuse), M as the default and the size for most cards, Small only on dense thumbnails (everywhere, recommended: a design rule the package doesn't check), Large on hero images, and the Don't against Small on a large card. avoidWhen keeps the two placement Don'ts (plain white surface, two hearts on one card); the guide names no component to use instead. Content good is the guide's three labels; there is no bad copy. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every toggle) and no Favorite Toggle Size M (the guide sets M everywhere, which only repeats the component's default); Size L only for the hero-image example, as the guide's Configuration gives it. isActive and onChange stand for the screen's wiring. The guide's In context places the toggle on a photo (a guide-kit Backdrop, CSS) above two Text lines; the example keeps only the toggle, since placing it over an image would need absolute-position style and the guide's backdrop is not a Coin component. FavoriteToggle is the only component used. Left out of examples: the anatomy and sizing specimens, the Small card, the Disabled and Loading specimens (SkeletonGroup has no entry in this pack) and the Don'ts. Consistency: only guidance/skeleton.json mentions FavoriteToggle (its notes: it reads the group, its own loading wins both ways, and a placeholder drawn by its own loading is a progressbar named Loading); that agrees with FavoriteToggle.tsx 174–175 and 223–233 and with this entry's loading rule. No other entry uses or names the toggle. Run on the installed build, 29 October, in headless Chrome (playwright-core, the guide's own page built with vite, react-native-web 0.21.2; script ft/run/tap.mjs in the batch scratch folder): the In context toggle is 29 × 29 with role switch and aria-checked false, a transparent container and a white heart; a click 5 px outside its right edge left it unsaved, a click inside saved it (aria-checked true, background rgb(255, 255, 255), heart rgb(206, 161, 90)); the Sizing specimens, shown at 1.5×, measure 21, 43.5 and 61.5 px (14, 29 and 41); the Disabled specimen has tabindex −1 and opacity 0.5. Sorting (batch 14, two cross-check runs). Round 1 flagged /placementAdvice/1 (generalises the In context card's top-right corner into a rule): our over-reading, so the item now says where the guide's In context card puts it. It flagged /facts/modes/2 and /configuration/1 for saying the size collection's own default is S, which the 0.1.78 evidence doesn't say (it is true in the package: the token file's default mode is S on dbe0e02, and FavoriteToggle.tsx says so at lines 70 and 95): our addition, so the evidence fact's description keeps to the evidence's words and the rule drops the clause. Its note called /configuration/9 (leave Favorite Toggle Color out of modes) an inference; it now says only what the fact says, that the collection follows isActive (FavoriteToggle.tsx 114–117 replaces a value passed in modes, and the building rules leave modes unset anyway). Rounds 1 and 2 flagged /facts/gaps/0 for naming dbe0e02 and the bug placeholder, which the evidence doesn't, and round 2 for “which phones honour”, which is the guide's Sizing and Sources copy rather than the evidence; dismissed in reviews/favoritetoggle.json with the source lines and the run above. Round 2's note asks a human to confirm loading on its own (the 0.1.60 evidence says it renders nothing): the installed source draws it (above), and the out-of-date evidence line is in the human flag. Left: the human flag (guide fix #538). Component Bug #541 (web tap area) for the coordinator to file or drop; the gap names it.
